title: FP8 / INT8 quantization profile calibration + long-context batch throughput/latency runbook
creator: Priya Malhotra
description:
Objective: Produce reproducible throughput and tail-latency benchmark artifacts and an operational runbook for FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants under long-context (>8k tokens) and multi-size batching workloads. This ticket covers calibration dataset selection, per-layer profile generation, evaluation of quantization-induced accuracy drift on representative prompt sets, and a bench matrix that isolates KV-cache behavior and warm/cold start tail-latency.

Background: Prior experiments (see ENG-24083 and ENG-26177) focused on batching sensitivity and calibration for medium context lengths. Customers running retrieval-augmented chat and long-document summarization have reported variable latency P95/P99 spikes when using INT8-like profiles with large prefix caching. We need a holistic calibration+benchmark plan that accounts for: dynamic prefix/KV cache hit patterns, per-layer outlier sensitivity, and realistic production traffic shapes (small bursts + a small fraction of very long requests).

Scope and deliverables:
- Calibration pipeline runs that produce per-layer FP8 and INT8 profiles for two model families (Llama-family 30B variant and a 70B baseline).
- A canonical calibration corpus documented (public datasets + internal telemetry-derived prompt traces) and transformation script for the calibration step.
- Benchmark matrix with axes: batch size (1/2/4/8/16), sequence length distribution (short-only, mixed, long-only 8k/16k/32k), KV-cache warm state (empty, 50% warm, fully warm), and concurrency (1, 4, 16).
- Measured metrics: throughput (tokens/s), latency P50/P95/P99, 99.9 tail insights, memory footprint, and accuracy deltas on targeted eval sets (dialogue, code, summarization).
- Runbook: step-by-step procedure to reproduce experiments, automated scripts, and guardrails (regression thresholds, rollback recommendations).

Approach and experiment plan:
1) Calibration dataset: curate a 15k-example calibration set mixing dialogue turns, code snippets, long-form documents (weights: 45% dialogue, 35% long-doc, 20% code). Document preprocessing steps (tokenization, chunking rules), and commit to an immutable calibration snapshot.
2) Per-layer calibration: run activation/statistics collection for FP8 and symmetric INT8 profiles across 128 calibration batches. For each run record per-layer max/mean/std and per-channel histograms. Generate profile artifacts and store in runtime-artifacts/quant-profiles/ENG-33210/.
3) Quant variants: produce two variants per model: FP8-default, INT8-symmetric, and a hybrid FP8-for-attn + INT8-for-ffn variant.
4) Bench harness: extend existing bench runner to: (a) replay telemetry-derived request traces, (b) toggle KV-cache initial state, (c) measure ordering of batching vs streaming effects. Ensure tokenization determinism and record token counts.
5) Accuracy validation: run the quantized variants on three eval suites (dialogue-quality, code-gen pass@1, long-doc summary ROUGE/L) and compute delta vs float32 baseline. Define acceptable thresholds: BLEU/ROUGE deltas <1.5 points and pass@1 drop <3%. Flag any prompt where model hallucination increases.
6) Stability and tail analysis: run 24-hour soak at synthetic traffic distribution to measure P99.9 and observe any degradation due to dynamic kernel selection or fragmentation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration pipeline reproducible end-to-end with artifacts checked into S3 and referenced in this ticket.
- Benchmark matrix completed and results documented in CSV + Kibana dashboard snapshot.
- Runbook with commands and scripts that allow on-call to reproduce a failing profile and fallback to safe variant in under 30 minutes.
- No accuracy metric regressions beyond thresholds; any failing prompts listed and triaged.

Risks and trade-offs:
- INT8 symmetric may reduce memory but can introduce per-channel outliers that blow up P99 latency under cache churn. We must capture these cases and decide whether to mask out problematic layers (FFN) or prefer hybrid strategy.
- FP8 profiling is sensitive to calibration corpus; overfitting the calibration set can hide tail numeric issues. Use mixed-domain calibration to mitigate.

Notes / links:
- Reference telemetry trace (internal): drive.google.com/drive/fake_trace_link
- Prior PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2412 (batcher improvements)
- Storage location (artifacts): s3://redwood-inference/quant-profiles/ENG-33210/

Next steps:
- RNG-seed and deterministic tokenization checks (Luca)
- Wiring bench harness KV-state toggles (Eng bench infra)
- Run FP8 calibration first; iterate INT8 after profile comparison
acceptance_criteria: 1) Artifacts for FP8 and INT8 profiles uploaded and checksum-verified. 2) Benchmark CSV and dashboard snapshots for all matrix cells exist. 3) Runbook tested by another engineer reproducing one cell end-to-end. 4) Accuracy deltas are within thresholds or failing prompts are added to an action sub-issue.
